name: remote_sha
title: SHA or version of a remote

origin.description: S3 generic for the commit SHA or package version of a remote.

arguments.text: Passed to the method. The GitHub method accepts use_curl.

origin.details: The default method returns NA_character_. A local directory reads Version from DESCRIPTION. A tarball returns NA_character_. A CRAN remote reads Version from the repository PACKAGES index for that name and package type. A GitHub remote asks the commits API for the ref.
origin.value: A length-1 character string, or NA_character_.
origin.example:
path <- tempfile()
dir.create(path)
writeLines(c("Package: foo", "Version: 1.0.0"), file.path(path, "DESCRIPTION"))
sha <- remotes:::remote_sha(remotes:::local_remote(path))
cat(paste0("remote_sha on a local directory with Version: 1.0.0 returns ", sha, ".\n"))

translation.description: S3 generic for the commit SHA or package version of a remote.

arguments.name: remote
arguments.text: A local_remote, cran_remote, or github_remote. Any other object uses the default.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: The GitHub method accepts use_curl and ignores it.

translation.details: The default method returns None, which is NA_character_. A local directory reads Version from DESCRIPTION. A tarball returns None. A CRAN remote fetches the text PACKAGES file for that repository and type and returns the trimmed Version. A GitHub remote calls the commits API the way github_commit does when curl is not used, and reads the JSON sha field. The request uses urllib.
translation.value: A string, or None for NA_character_.
translation.example:
import os
import tempfile
from remotes.remote import local_remote, remote_sha
path = tempfile.mkdtemp()
with open(os.path.join(path, "DESCRIPTION"), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
    handle.write("Package: foo\nVersion: 1.0.0\n")
sha = remote_sha(local_remote(path))
print("remote_sha on a local directory with Version: 1.0.0 returns " + sha + ".")
